KeyTheme: Creation, the Fall, and God's covenant with the patriarchs
Summary: Genesis tells how God created the world, how sin entered through the Fall, and how God began His rescue plan through covenants with Noah, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. It follows the patriarchs and ends with Jacob's family settled in Egypt, setting the stage for the Exodus.
KeyPeople: Adam; Eve; Noah; Abraham; Sarah; Isaac; Jacob; Joseph
Purpose: To show Israel its origins and that the God who created all things chose Abraham's family to bless all nations.
Outline: Creation and the Fall (1-11); Abraham (12-25); Isaac and Jacob (26-36); Joseph (37-50)
HistoricalContext: Written for Israel after the Exodus, looking back to primeval history and the patriarchal age in Canaan and Egypt, roughly 2000-1800 BC for the patriarchs.
